questions.stem: From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one represented by the letters underlined: s**ea**t
questions.explanation: Seat has the long pure vowel /iː/. Beat shares that sound. Sit has the short vowel /i/, which is a different phoneme, not a shorter version of the same one. Length is part of the identity of the vowel.

distractorRationale.a: Sit is /i/, the classic short partner of /iː/, and the most common trap
distractorRationale.b: Set has /e/, a different short vowel
distractorRationale.d: Sat has /æ/, a different short vowel

questions.stem: Which word has the same vowel sound as sit?
questions.explanation: Sit has short /i/. The first vowel of women is also /i/, despite the letter o. Machine, receive and people all have long /iː/. Matching the letter i in sit to the letter i in machine is the spelling trap this item is built on.

distractorRationale.a: Machine has /iː/, as in seat, not sit
distractorRationale.c: Receive has /iː/ in the second syllable
distractorRationale.d: People has /iː/, another long-vowel spelling of the seat family

questions.stem: Which word contains a diphthong?
questions.explanation: Boy has /ɔɪ/, a closing diphthong: the tongue glides from an /ɔ/-like start toward /i/ inside one syllable. Seat /iː/, sit /i/ and bird /ɜː/ are pure vowels; the tongue does not glide.

distractorRationale.a: Seat is a long pure vowel /iː/, not a glide
distractorRationale.b: Sit is a short pure vowel /i/
distractorRationale.d: Bird is the long pure vowel /ɜː/

questions.stem: From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one represented by the letters underlined: gr**ea**t
